title: GPU context eviction & page-faults under mixed Llama/Mistral/Qwen long-context workloads
body:
Summary:

This note collects experiments and observations from a recurring class of tail-latency spikes we see when serving mixed-model workloads (small-medium model families: Llama-2-13B fp16, Mistral-large int8-ish kernels, Qwen-2-7B fp16) on a shared GPU pool with long-context requests (4k-32k tokens). The spikes (10-30x over median per-token) are intermittent and correlate with high system-level GPU page-faults and CUDA context eviction messages in dmesg. Hypothesis: mixing different model kernels + MoE routing churn + sporadic long-context requests causes memory fragmentation and repeated CUDA context switching/eviction which forces expensive page migrations or kernel re-instantiation, producing tail latency.

Why this matters:
- Customer facing p99s for streaming endpoints spike unpredictably under multi-tenant mixes.
- Observed when we co-locate MoE inference (routing topk=2, 64 experts) alongside dense models on the same physical GPU nodes.
- Standard CPU-side batching/queueing hides the root cause; need GPU-level fixes to avoid cost inflation and SLA breaches.

Environment / baseline config used for experiments:
- Hardware: AWS p4d.24xlarge equivalent (A100-80GB nodes) and a set of internal DGX-A100 80GB hosts used for stress tests.
- Runtime: redwood-runtime v1.18.2 (kernel selection + quantization heuristics enabled).
- CUDA: 11.8, driver 525.x, cuDNN 8.4.
- Models: Llama-2-13B fp16 (hf-llama-13b), Mistral-large with int8 kernels (hf-mistral-large-int8), Qwen-2-7B fp16.
- MoE setup: Llama variant instrumented with router gating (topk=2, 64 experts distributed across GPUs using our sharded-expert allocator).
- Workloads: synthetic mix generator that emits 70% short (<=256 tokens) requests, 25% medium (2k-4k), 5% long (8k-32k). Mixed concurrency 80-200 qps across node.

Observed signals and reproducible traces:
- dmesg / kernel logs: frequent lines with "NVRM: GPU at .. has fallen off the bus" NOT present, but repeated messages of "GPU context preemption" and "GPU page fault" around spike times.
- nvprof / Nsight traces: shows intermittent long gaps where no GPU kernels execute (~30-150ms) while CPU threads are waiting on cudaStreamSynchronize. During those gaps, memory copy kernels appear to be re-mapping large allocations.
- nvidia-smi pmon: shows rapid jumps in GPU memory utilization between model loads; memory peaks correspond to long-context requests hitting max KV cache allocations.
- runtime tracer: kernel selection path re-evaluated (quantization->fp16 fallback) when previously-evicted model blobs are re-initialized, adding 25-80ms of one-off penalty.
- perf and system metrics: increased host-side page faults (anon) when Unified Memory fallbacks are used under fragmentation.

Root-cause analysis (working hypothesis):
1) Memory fragmentation + transient KV cache peaks: long-context requests allocate large KV caches and temporary buffers. When multiple different model binaries/kernels with different memory layout requirements are used, the GPU allocator fragments.
2) Context eviction for kernel reconfiguration: our runtime frequently creates short-lived CUDA execution contexts for quantized kernels (int8 conversions) and uses kernel caching. Under memory pressure, driver evicts contexts to reclaim VRAM, causing subsequent requests to incur context re-creation and module (cuModuleLoad) overhead.
3) Page migration & Unified Memory fallbacks: in some cases the allocator falls back to using UVM or triggers page migration, observed as GPU page-faults and host<->device stalls. UVM migration latency is large (tens to hundreds of ms) and produces tail spikes.
4) MoE routing churn amplifies allocations: routing causes fanout to multiple experts; when experts are distributed across GPUs, routing induces small bursts of inter-GPU NCCL traffic and transient allocations for intermediate buffers, increasing chance of fragmentation and eviction.

Quick experiments that support this chain:
- Isolate long-context only on a dedicated node: spikes disappear.
- Isolate mixed-model (no MoE) on same node: intermittent but lower amplitude spikes (suggesting MoE amplifies problem).
- Pre-warm all model blobs and keep a persistent CUDA context pool: reduces spike frequency by ~60% in experiments.
- Turn off UVM fallbacks (force OOM if no memory): spikes convert into hard OOMs, confirming some spikes were due to UVM migration.
- Replace dynamic kernel loading with monolithic precompiled kernels for int8 paths: one-off reconfig costs reduced but not eliminated, implying both fragmentation and context preemption contribute.

Mitigations and operational recommendations (short term):
- Co-location policy: avoid mixing MoE-serving GPUs with dense-model serving on same node for workloads with >2% long-context requests. Implement isolation rule in scheduler.
- Preload & pin model artifacts: keep model code + kernels resident across allocations (persistent cuda context pool). Add warmup traffic on node boot / scale-up.
- Memory pooling: switch to cudaMallocAsync / memory pool allocator to prevent fragmentation; allocate large contiguous KV cache arenas per-GPU.
- Prefer exclusive-expert placement: collocate experts for an MoE shard to reduce inter-GPU transient buffers and NCCL fanouts.
- Avoid UVM fallbacks for latency-critical paths: prefer explicit allocation failures over unpredictable UVM migration; fail fast and retry on different node.
- Kernel-homogeneity scheduling: group models with same kernel types (fp16 vs int8) onto same GPU groups to avoid repeated module loads.

Longer-term runtime changes to explore:
- Implement a lightweight 'context-lease' mechanism to pin bundles of kernels and memory ranges per-tenant for configurable durations.
- Deeper integration with CUDA memory advice APIs to reserve address space and avoid host migration.
- Proactive background defragmentation: off-peak compaction using large scratch allocations + copy, similar to allocator compaction.
- Static expert packing: scheduler pack experts that are often co-activated into the same GPU to reduce runtime fanout.
- Telemetry: add a high-cardinality metric for "cuda-context-evictions" and GPU page-fault counts per-node exposed to console to trigger auto-evacuations.

Short runbook for on-call (repro steps / immediate remediation):
1) If p99/process latency spikes and dmesg shows GPU page-faults: temporarily drain node from serving and set autoscaler to shift traffic.
2) Check runtime tracer: look for repeated cuModuleLoad / context creation events.
3) Try forcing model pinning (cron job available: tools/warmup/pin-models.sh) to reduce reinitialization.
4) If spikes persist and UVM events present, taint node in scheduler with tag "no-uvm" and mark for maintenance to run compaction.
5) Open JIRA-ENG-1198 to track root cause artifacts, attach Nsight traces.

Planned experiments next:
- Controlled fragmentation inject: allocate / free sequences to reproduce page-faults without real model logic. Measure fragmentation threshold.
- Expert packing ablation: run identical workload with experts co-located vs spread and compare p99.
- Vary quantization kernel mix: force all int8 kernels precompiled vs mixed and measure context-init costs.
- Test cudaMallocAsync with large arena vs baseline allocator on A100-80GB.

Notes / open questions:
- We haven't reproduced the event on Ampere-40GB variants consistently; hypothesis: 80GB allows larger UVM fallbacks so latency effect is visible only there.
- Driver upgrades (CUDA 12.x) may change eviction behavior; need gated test before rolling.
- Need to quantify the cost tradeoff between isolated nodes (underutilization) vs complexity of context pinning.

Appendix: useful commands / traces to collect
- dmesg | grep -i -E "page fault|evict|preempt|cuda"
- sudo nsight-systems --trace=cuda,osrt -o /tmp/trace.qns <pid>
- nvprof / nsys sampling of kernel load times and cuModuleLoad durations
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 1
- runtime trace: RUNTIME_TRACER=1 ./bin/runtime --node-id $NODE collect-trace

If useful I can paste a trimmed Nsight .qns timeline for the 2024-10-24 spike we captured (attached to the linked GH PR), and we should probably onboard SRE to schedule a driver upgrade test matrix.

---
Notes to self: follow up with Marco on experiment harness fixes (linear://lr/serving/472) so we can re-run with quantization-only kernels precompiled. Also file a short RFC for context-lease design by end-November.
